assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a finished editorial book-cover illustration for Tomorrow's Newspaper, a thoughtful technical essay about building a machine to read annual reports, then discovering the danger of hindsight. Portrait A4-like ratio, at least 1600 px tall. A quiet tall reading room at night, seen in elegant slightly isometric cutaway perspective. In the lower two thirds: a long desk, a non-humanoid optical reading instrument part telescope part reading lamp, with a large teal glass lens, aimed at an open dense annual report. Two thick stacks of bound annual reports nearby; a distinctly folded newspaper lies beside the report. The instrument's translucent lens subtly reflects the newspaper rather than just the report, an ambiguous suggestion of knowledge leaking from another time. Tall indigo windows, amber desk lamp pool, calm thoughtful atmosphere, precise ink outlines with sophisticated flat color and fine risograph paper grain. Limited palette ink #1F2A37, teal #0F766E and #5FB3AB, indigo #4C5FD5, amber #E8A33D, pale cool paper #F7F8FA. NO brown or sepia cast. Top 38 percent almost entirely pale paper with very faint architectural contours, quiet negative space for separate dark title typography. Bottom 8 percent quiet pale paper for author credit. Full bleed composition, deliberate spaciousness, not a generic fintech advertisement. NO text, letters, numbers, logos, stock chart, humanoid robot, trophy, magical glowing brain, bull or bear. Newspaper and annual report typography should be abstract fine rules only. Artwork must read at printed A4 scale. No border.

Deliberate elegant composition, readable at 6.27 inches wide, not photorealistic or a 3D render. No logos, invented data, words, letters or numbers. Keep a 4% safe margin. Subject: a modest nocturnal print workshop in an architectural cutaway. From left to right, envelopes arrive at a door, three indigo browser-like printing presses turn filings into paper, and a teal optical reading instrument at a desk reads a report. At back a tidy pegboard has exactly five rows of five key hooks (keys are a motif, no numeric labels), some occupied some empty, beside a clerk's open ledger with tidy folders. A tiny phone on a shelf has a single amber notification dot. One simplified human artisan clears paper from one stalled press. The dominant high wall clock has plain tick marks and hands showing a few minutes before midnight; this is a factory that must wait. Architecture compact and humane, not a giant industrial plant. Pale cool walls, amber lamps, teal instrument, indigo machinery. No numerical claims in image. Entire scene visible, no title space needed.
assets.edit_prompt: Edit only two details in this finished workshop illustration. The wall clock must have exactly two hands showing 11:57: short hour hand just to the left of 12 at the very top, long minute hand pointing between 11 and 12 closer to 11. No third hand, no numerals, no text. It should clearly feel like a few minutes before midnight, not 11 o'clock. No other changes.
